How to use
Redlining an RFDS, end to end
  • The ribbon is grouped by job: File · Edit · Redline tools · Text · Arrange · Assist · Find · View. The strip underneath shows the active tool, the mark count, save state, and the last message.
  • Redline: click any text cell to drop an editable red overlay pre-filled with that cell's exact value, so a count, status, or model becomes editable red text sitting on top. After one mark the tool switches to Select so you don't keep stamping. Right-click anywhere adds a redline and keeps the tool armed — on a cell it copies the value, on blank space it starts empty.
  • Strike row strikes a whole row (removed/decommissioned). Strike text strikes one value, or drag for a horizontal strike. Line draws a free horizontal line. Strikes and lines are always horizontal; click one to select it, then drag its blue end handles to resize.
  • Select: click to select, drag a box over blank space to marquee-select (this catches strikes as well as text), Shift/Ctrl+click to add or remove one mark, and Shift-drag to pan when zoomed in.
  • Moving several marks at once: any multi-selection drags as one rigid block — text redlines and strikes together — and so does a group. Select two or more marks and press Ctrl+G (or ⛓ Group) to make the grouping stick; after that, dragging any member moves the whole group. Ctrl+Shift+G ungroups. Grouping a strike with its replacement text is the quickest way to keep a correction together.
  • With two or more marks selected, a toolbar appears above them to align edges or centers, space evenly (3+ marks), match font size to the largest, group, or delete. ⬚ All on page (Ctrl+A) selects every mark on the page you're viewing; Esc clears the selection.
  • Zoom: the ＋/− buttons, ⤢ Fit to fit the window, or hold Ctrl and scroll the wheel over the page (this keeps the point under the cursor).
  • Appearance: ◐ Theme in View opens a picker — Night, Day or System (follow the operating system), plus seventeen colour themes shown as swatches — some a blend of two colours, some a straight two-colour combination. D flips night/day directly. The page itself always stays white and redlines stay red in every theme, so a mark reads the same whatever you pick; your choice is remembered between sessions.
  • Discrepancies is a read-only tab that compares every equipment model across Design Summary, RF Inventory, Equipment in Calc and Antenna Position, and flags what disagrees: a model missing from a table that should carry it, a quantity that does not match, one model printed two ways, or one model typed two ways. The table is computed from the grids, so it is exact. ▤ Explain these asks Claude to write a report about that table — the table is the record, the report is the commentary.
  • Sectors: the sector cell on a Design Summary row is a dropdown of the standard letters plus ✎ Type a value… for anything else — A,B,C, ALL, a carrier label. A typed value is stamped exactly as written.
  • Analyze RFDS opens a chooser first: every section it detected and how many pages each has. Nothing is read until you pick — untick what you do not need, or narrow to a page range, then Read the selected pages — everything is ticked to begin with. Detection itself is free, so the page numbers are real before you commit. What it reads goes into editable grids, and only what you change gets stamped. ↻ Re-analyze widens the scope later. Mirror from CDs imports a redlined Construction-Drawing PDF and reports where it differs from the RFDS; Apply CD findings then stamps those differences as editable marks.
  • Fill As-Built copies Design values into the blank As-Built cells on Antenna Position Details (Final) pages.
  • Existing and Proposed Decommission pages are locked — the analyze tools never mark them (their rail entry and page label show "locked").
  • The left page rail turns red for pages that have marks; click a number to jump. ▤ Marks lists every redline to click through or delete.
  • Redline PDF keeps the original pages intact (vector, not flattened) and adds the redlines as Times New Roman annotations — and embeds the data, so you can reopen the exported file here and keep editing.
  • Shortcuts: S Select · R Redline · W Strike row · C Copy row · T Strike text · L Line · F Find · M Marks · D day/night · Ctrl+S save · Ctrl+E export · Ctrl+A select page · Ctrl+G group · Ctrl+D duplicate · Ctrl+Z/Y undo/redo · arrow keys nudge (Shift for a bigger step) · Delete removes the selection.
